Ts Nyi Pao （朱二宝）
Haining // D.S.I. Lee Shu Fah
C. B. H. Q. 3-10-41

My name is Ts Nyi Pao, age 41, native of Yah Zah
Village, Haining.

I live with my husband Tsu Tsoong Ziang (朱忠祥)
in Yah Zah. On or about the 1st of September 1941 I met
two persons named Sih and Wong in a tea shop in Yah Zah
and during the ensuing conversation we discussed the
transporting of furs from Yah Zah to Shanghai for sale;
however, no definite arrangement was made.

Two or three days later I met Wong again and it was
decided that he and I should each raise half of the capital
for the purpose of dealing in furs. Wong eventually brought
to me $5,500 as his share, of which $500 was contributed
by one Tsaung Nyien Kiang (章江). I raised $5,700 from
the following sources :-

Myself $300
Zung Foh Kwei (陳福貴) $1000
Female Woo $500
13 others @ $300 each $3900

Of this $5,700.00, $200 was kept aside under my
care as being surplus.

On 12/9/41 we bought 600 pieces of sheep skin for
$9,600 and had them packed into eight small parcels. On the
same day I, together with three others named Lee Nyi Man
(李二毛), Sung Ah Nyi (沈阿二) and Tsang Ah Soong (張阿松)
brought the furs on to the train at Yah Zah and left the
latter place for Shanghai. When we brought the furs to the
train we did so when the Japanese soldier on duty was
pages.zh:
Ts Nyi Pao （朱二宝）
海宁 // 副督察 李树法
刑事科总部 1941年10月3日

我叫 Ts Nyi Pao，41岁，籍贯海宁鸦扎村（Yah Zah Village）。

我与丈夫 Tsu Tsoong Ziang（朱忠祥）居住在鸦扎。1941年9月1日左右，我在鸦扎的一家茶馆遇到了名为 Sih 和 Wong 的两人，在随后的交谈中，我们讨论了将皮草从鸦扎运往上海出售的事宜；然而，并未达成确切安排。

两三天后，我再次遇到 Wong，决定由他和我也各筹集一半资金用于皮草生意。Wong 最终给我带来了他那份的5,500元，其中500元由 Tsaung Nyien Kiang（章江）出资。我从以下来源筹集了5,700元：-

我自己 $300
Zung Foh Kwei（陳福貴） $1000
吴女士 $500
其他13人 @ 每人$300 $3900

在这5,700.00元中，有200元作为盈余由我保管。

1941年9月12日，我们以9,600元购买了600张羊皮，并将它们打包成八个小包裹。同日，我与另外三人 Lee Nyi Man（李二毛）、Sung Ah Nyi（沈阿二）和 Tsang Ah Soong（張阿松）一起，在鸦扎将皮草带上火车，离开该地前往上海。我们将皮草带上火车时，正值当值的日本士兵

pages.en:
- 2 -

temporarily absent, for we knew that such acts were not
allowed by the Japanese Authorities.

When the train reached Sungkiang, Tsaung Nyien
Kiang joined us and had the furs made into two packs.
When nearing Shanghai, he threw the two packs of furs
overboard from the moving train. What happened to the
furs afterwards I do not know.

I and Lee, Sung and Tsang returned to Yah Zah on
13/9/41 and on the same day brought another lot of furs
to Shanghai in the same manner as described above.

Since then I have been staying at the Cha Woo
lodging house, Fokien Road till the time of my arrest on
17/9/41.

Lee, Sung and Tsang returned to Yah Zah on 14/9/41.

Signed :-
pages.zh:
- 2 -

暂时不在场，因为我们知道日本当局不允许此类行为。

当火车到达松江时，Tsaung Nyien Kiang 加入我们要行列，并将皮草重新打成两个大包。当接近上海时，他将这两包皮草从行驶中的火车上扔了下去。此后皮草的下落我便不知晓了。

我、Lee、Sung 和 Tsang 于1941年9月13日返回鸦扎，并于同日以如上所述的方式将另一批皮草运往上海。

此后我一直住在福建路的 Cha Woo 旅馆，直到1941年9月17日被捕。

Lee、Sung 和 Tsang 于1941年9月14日返回鸦扎。

签名 :-

The 2nd named states she arrived in Shanghai from
Haining on Monday 15-9-41 for the purpose of buying under-

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie Re recovery
of stolen property.

At 3.50 p.m. on the 26th September 1941 Sergeant
Fujita of the Japanese Gendarmerie accompanied by a
prisoner named Sung Kou Minn (孫國祥) age 22, native
of Hanchow, called at H.Q.O.B. (C.I.) and requested
assistance to visit a pawn shop in the vicinity of
Canton-Fokien Roads where to recover a gentleman's jacket
which had been stolen from a Japanese named Nagamura,
Jinkee Road, C.O.L. by the prisoner and pawned by him
on the 14-9-41 on a sum of $10.00.

At 4 p.m. the prisoner led D.S.I.s Konovaloff,
Lee Shu Fah and the Gendarme to the Zoh Sing (佐兴) Pawn
Shop, at 68 Se Sang Ling, off Canton Road where the
property in question, bearing the name of the complainant
(Japanese characters embroidered on the inside left pocket)
was recovered. Redemption fee was paid by the Gendarmerie
and the recovered jacket was handed over to Sergeant
Fujita.

Further to:-Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 4 p.m. on the 30th September 1941 Sub
Lieut. Katoda and four other members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie accompanied by the arrested manager Lo
Lung Chih called again at C.I. offices and requested
further assistance to search the Ming Sung Industrial
Co.'s offices.

Between the hours of 4.15 p.m. to 5.15 p.m.
on the 30-9-41 and 2.30 p.m. and 4 p.m. on the 1st
October 1941, the offices in question were searched
including four safes; the keys were produced by the
manager, and as a result six filing covers containing
correspondence and a number of cablegrams were seized.
No seizure effected from the safes.
The contents of the seizure is being now
examined by D.S.I. Lee.

Sub Lieut. Katoda made a request that the seized documents be handed over to the Gendarmerie.
He also requested that the offices of the
Ming Sung Industrial Co. be locked and the keys kept
at C.I. offices, until the enquiries conducted by the
Japanese Gendarmerie are concluded.

This request was acceded to. Instructions
regarding the handing over of the seized documents are

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 8 a.m. on the 27th September 1941 Sub-Lieutenant
Katoda and four other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
called at H.C.C.R. C.I. offices and requested assistance
to visit an address at 180 Ningpo Road wherein to carry
out a search of an office of one named Lo Lung Chih
(羅龍芝) who had been arrested by the Gendarmerie in
the French Concession with assistance of Det. Inspector
Maron of the French Police prior to the request of this
assistance.

Sub-Lieutenant Katoda stated that Lo Lung Chih
was suspected of anti-Japanese activities and acting as
a manager of the Ming Sung Industrial Co. (民生實業公司),
180 Ningpo Road, he supplied the Chinese National Govern-
ment with war materials and that some documents substan-
tiating his information could be found in the office of
Lo Lung Chih.

Necessary assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Lee
Shu Fah, C.D.C.s 57 and 201, D.I. Kobayashi and the
undersigned who together with the Gendarmes visited the
office in question at 8.20 a.m.

Upon arrival at the address noted it was found that
the Ming Sung Industrial Co. occupied two rooms situated

协助日本宪兵队

1941年9月27日上午8时，加藤（Katoda，音译）少尉及另外四名日本宪兵队成员来到总部刑事调查处办公室，请求协助前往宁波路180号的一个地址，对名为罗龙芝（羅龍芝）的一人的办公室进行搜查，该人此前在法租界被捕，当时是在法国警察马伦（Maron，音译）巡官的协助下，应本次协助请求之前由宪兵队实施的逮捕。

加藤少尉称，罗龙芝涉嫌从事反日活动，并作为宁波路180号民生实业公司（民生實業公司）的经理，向中国政府提供军用物资，且在罗龙芝的办公室中可以找到证实这一情报的一些文件。

刑事调查处副督察长李树发（Lee Shu Fah，音译）、中国侦探警员57号和201号、小林（Kobayashi，音译）巡官以及签署人提供了必要的协助，并与宪兵一同于上午8时20分前往上述办公室。

到达上述地址后发现，民生实业公司占用位于

pages.en:
1/2

on the 3rd floor. These two rooms used as offices were
found to be locked at the time. An office boy produced
the keys and opened the offices.

On entering the offices it was observed that all
filing cabinets including four safes were also locked.
In view of this it was suggested to Sub-Lieutenant
Katoda that the arrested manager be produced in person
as without his presence the office could not be searched.

To this suggestion Sub-Licut. Katoda indicated
that the manager had not been handed over to him yet
and that he was expecting to have the manager in his
custody in next few hours and requested a watch to be
maintained in the offices.

This request was complied with and the watch
was maintained until 12.40 p.m. when the Gendarmerie
requested to withdraw the watch and that the offices in
question be locked and the keys kept by the S.M.Police
until the Japanese Gendarmerie secured the handing over
of the manager from the custody of the French Police.

This request was, likewise, complied with and
the keys are being kept in the H.Q.C.B. C.I. offices
pending further developments.

A. Konovaloff
D. S. I.

1/2

三楼的两个房间。这两个用作办公室的房间当时发现是锁着的。一名办公室勤杂工拿出钥匙打开了办公室。

进入办公室后，观察到所有文件柜，包括四个保险箱，也都锁着。鉴于此情况，向加藤少尉建议，应将已被捕的经理亲自带至现场，因为若无他在场，无法对办公室进行搜查。

对于此建议，加藤少尉表示，经理尚未移交给他们，他预计在接下来的几个小时内能将经理置于其 custody（监管）之下，并请求在办公室维持监视。

此请求已获遵行，监视一直持续到下午12时40分，此时宪兵队要求撤除监视，并将上述办公室锁闭，钥匙由上海公共租界工部局警务处保管，直到日本宪兵队从法国警察的监管下获得经理的移交。

此请求同样已获遵行，钥匙正存放在总部刑事调查处办公室，以待后续发展。

A. Konovaloff

Further to: Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

On 11-10-41 the 1st accused named Tong Er was returned to the custody of the S.M. Police together with Letter Shankenko No. 928/41 requesting the permanent handing over of this man and setting out the evidence against him.

A statement has been taken from this accused in which he admits that since 1939 he has acted as mayor of Chuen Shah Hsien, Pootung, under the Kiangsu Provincial Government which functions under the Chungking Regime. He has lived in the French Concession during this period and never visited Chuen Shah Hsien, his only duty being to keep records for which he received a salary of $60.00 per month. He received his salary from one named Ting Chu Zung, who was the executive Superintendant and when this man was arrested by the Japanese he destroyed all the records.

A translation of the statement is attached together with a translation of the seized documents, some of which are incriminating and include a report on guerrilla activities in Pootung.

Tong Er (唐屹) alias Yao Yue (耀與)
) alias Dien Lih zung (田立人)
Nanwei, Kiangsu // C.D.S. 69
C.B.H.Q. 13-10-41 translated Clerk Y.C. Chang
xxxxxxx

Tong Er alias Yao Yue alias Dien Lih zung, age 51
years, native of Nanwei, Kiangsu, married, and residing at House
3 Lane 248 Route Prelupt, French Concession.

At the age of 5 I studied in a private school for 10
years. When I was 15 years old I attended the Kiangsu Military
Primary School and the Hupei Preliminary School, 2nd branch, up
to the age of 25, then I studied in the Paoting Military College
from which I was later graduated.

Since the year 1939 I have been employed as the
mayor of Chuen Shah Hsien, Pootung by one named Heu Tuh Jing, the
chairman of Kiangsu Provincial Government under the Chungking
Regime. My only duty is for the safe keeping of the official
chops and documents. Since my employment on this mentioned duty
I have lived in the French Concession, Shanghai, and have never
visited Chuen Shah, Pootung. The documents, which were kept for
safe, were destroyed by me, after Ping Chu Zung, the Executive
Superintendent, had been arrested by the Japanese.

The constitution of this city is as follows:- One
mayor, one secretary, one clerk, one messenger and one orderly.
The total monthly expenses for our organization was $267.00
which was paid to us monthly by Ping Chu Zung, the Executive
Superintendent. Of the said sum of money, I monthly received
$50.00, Chu Koong Dai, the secretary, $40.00, Zi Tsung Chuen, the
clerk, $25.00, Sung Ta Chuen, the messenger $20.00 and an orderly
$12.00. The remainder sum of money was used for postages and
other expenses.

On the 3-10-41 whilst staying in Room 101 of the 2nd

刑事科总部 1941年10月13日 翻译员：张YC（Y.C. Chang）
xxxxxxx

唐屹，又名耀與，又名田立人，51岁，江苏南汇人，已婚，居住在法租界普鲁普特路（Route Prelupt，音译）248弄3号。

5岁时我在私塾读书10年。15岁时我就读于江苏陆军小学和湖北预备学校第二分校，直至25岁，随后我在保定军校学习，后来从中毕业。

自1939年以来，我一直受雇于许图景（Heu Tuh Jing，音译），担任重庆政权管辖下的江苏省政府主席委任的浦东川沙县县长。我唯一的职责是妥善保管官方印章和文件。自从受聘担任上述职务以来，我一直居住在上海法租界，从未去过浦东川沙。在丁楚宗（Ping Chu Zung，音译，注：此处名字拼写与前文Ting Chu Zung略有不同，依原文译出）执行主管被日本人逮捕后，我将代为保管的文件销毁。

本县政府的构成如下：一名县长，一名秘书，一名职员，一名信差和一名勤务兵。我们机构的每月总支出为267.00美元，由执行主管丁楚宗（Ping Chu Zung，音译）按月支付给我们。在上述款项中，我每月领取50.00美元，秘书朱公岱（Chu Koong Dai，音译）40.00美元，职员资宗全（Zi Tsung Chuen，音译）25.00美元，信差宋达全（Sung Ta Chuen，音译）20.00美元，勤务兵12.00美元。剩余款项用于邮资和其他开支。

1941年10月3日，当我住在亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road，即今淮海中路）大华旅馆（Loh Hotel，音译）101室时，为了叫医生来看病，我被警察逮捕，随后被移交到西区捕房。
上述供词与我在西区捕房所作的供词相似。

At 7.20 a.m. on 3-10-41 Sergeant Major Inoyi
and two other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
accompanied by two Chinese assistants came to C.B.H.Q.
and requested assistance to visit Room 101 of the Dah
Loh Hotel, 89 Yu Ye Ching Road to arrest one named
Tong (唐 ), the Chief of a Guerilla Unit operating in
Peotung.

Assistance was rendered by D.I.s Pryde and Kobayashi
D.S.I. Yang Shih Kwang, C.D.C. 211 and the stated
address visited where the following were arrested :-

(1) Tong Er (唐屹), 51, Nanwei, M/Mayer
of Nanwei City.
(2) Tong Tsang Sz (唐張氏), 34, Nanwei, M/Wife
of 1st accused.
(3) Weng Shing Sung (王生), 38, Peotung,
M/Tailor, 124 Yu Yuen Road.
(4) Sung Chang (宋張), 31, Peotung, M Bird
salesman.

The 1st accused admits being the mayor of Nanwei
City under the Chungking Regime. Up till two weeks ago
he was living at House 3 Lane 148 Route Prolupt when
he received a letter warning him that the Japanese
wanted to arrest him, so has since then been living
in various hotels together with his wife, the 2nd

普赖德（Pryde，音译）巡官、小林（Kobayashi，音译）巡官、杨世光（Yang Shih Kwang，音译）副督察长、中国侦探警员211号提供了协助，并前往上述地址，逮捕了以下人员：-

(1) 唐屹（Tong Er），51岁，南汇人，男/南汇市市长。

(4) 宋张（Sung Chang），31岁，浦东人，男/鸟贩。

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 6 a.m. 4-10-41 Sergeant Morishita accompanied by other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters came to Crime Branch Headquarters (C.I.) and requested assistance to visit 76 Hwakee Avenue, E/Well Road for purpose of effecting the arrest of the occupants of room No. 7, it being alleged that they were members of a Chinese Guerrilla Unit.

Necessary arrangements having been made with the U.S. Marine Corp and E/Well Station the desired assistance was rendered by D.I. Crighton, D.S. Semeshima, D.I. Soong Ping Tsung and C.D.C. 211.

On arrival at the address in question it was ascertained that Room No. 7 was occupied by one:-

Tsung Yang Pah (程雍伯) age 28, Soochow, M/Partner in the Dah Peh (大华) Native Bank located in the French Concession.

A search of this room revealed nothing of an incriminating nature, however at the request of Sergeant Morishita the above said person was brought to Crime Branch H.Q. he having admitted knowing the whereabouts of one named:- Lee Kyeong Kang (李荣刚) wanted by the Gendarmerie for being concerned in Guerrilla activities.

1941年10月4日上午6时，森下警部伴同日本宪兵队总部其他成员来到刑事处总部（C.I.），请求协助前往爱威尔路（E/Well Road）华琪路76号，目的是逮捕7号房间的居住者，据称他们是中国游击队的成员。

在与美国海军陆战队及爱威尔路捕房作出必要安排后，由督察克里顿（Crighton）、副督察世岛（Semeshima）、督察宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）及华人侦探长211号提供了所需协助。

抵达上述地址后，查明7号房间由以下一人居住：

程雍伯（Tsung Yang Pah），28岁，苏州人，男，系位于法租界的大华银行合伙人。

对该房间的检查未发现任何具有罪证性质的物品，但应森下警部的要求，将上述人员带至刑事处总部，因其承认知晓一名叫李荣刚（Lee Kyeong Kang）者的下落，此人因涉嫌参与游击活动而被宪兵队通缉。

Headquarters
C.l. sc.207/41.    Crime Branch
                   7th October             41.

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie
re arrest of Educational leaders of
Chungking Government.

At 6 a.m. October 6, 1941, Sergeant Major
Kurouji of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters attended
Crime Branch Headquarters (C.l.) together with three
other members and a male in custody named Tsung Tah Keng
(陳達康) 34, native Manchuria, whom they had arrested
on 5-10-41 in the French Concession as being a member of
the Educational group, Shanghai branch, of the Chungking
Government advocating continued resistance to the Japanese.
He had admitted this and implicated two others named
1. Wong Kung Tsung (王昌仲) alias Yien Ming (葉明) and
2. Chang Tsu Hing (蔣秋英) as also belonging to the
same group.
He allegedly did not know their addresses
but gave Lane 400 House 4 Peking Road as an accommodation
address.

Assistance was rendered by D.S. Sugimoto,
D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung, C.B.S. 62, C.B.C. 211 and the
undersigned at 8.30 a.m. when this address was visited.
Nothing incriminating was found there but a cook named
Tsen Foo Woo (朱福華) 58, Canton, stated he knew one
named Tsiang (蒋) residing Lane 39 House 18 North Kiangsi
Road who visited the Peking Road address frequently.

（左侧手写批注：S.J. / 4.10.41.）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI / MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / 7 OCT 1941）
（左侧手写编号：998110）
（左侧手写批注：b.q.o. / 10/10）

1

协助日本宪兵队逮捕重庆政府教育界领袖。

1941年10月6日上午6时，日本宪兵队总部的黑路治（Kurouji）警部率其他三名成员及一名被拘留男子陈達康（Tsung Tah Keng）来到刑事处总部（C.l.）。该男子34岁，满洲籍，他们于1941年10月5日在法租界以其为重庆政府教育部上海分部成员、主张继续抗日为由将其逮捕。他已承认此事，并供出另外两人，即1. 王昌仲（Wong Kung Tsung），别名叶明（Yien Ming），以及2. 蔣秋英（Chang Tsu Hing），也属于同一团体。据称他不知道他们的地址，但提供了北京路400弄4号作为通讯地址。

上午8时30分，由副督察杉本（Sugimoto）、副督察夏维方（Zia Vai Faung）、华人侦探副手62号、华人侦探长211号及签署人提供协助，前往该地址。在那里未发现任何罪证，但一名叫朱福華（Tsen Foo Woo）的厨师，58岁，广东人，称他认识一名姓蒋（Tsiang）的人，居住在江西北路39弄18号，此人经常光顾北京路的地址。

（左侧手写批注：S.J. / 1941年10月4日。）
（左侧印章：上海 / 公共租界警务处 / 特务科 / 1941年10月7日）
（左侧手写编号：998110）
（左侧手写批注：b.q.o. / 10/10）

pages.en:

A visit was paid to Lane 59/18 North Kiangse
Road at 7.30 a.m. and the male Tsiang Vung (鄭文)
located. He proved to be a Customs broker and had
visited the Peking Road address on business only.
The party withdrew, no arrests or seizures being made.

At the request of the Gendarmerie, the cook
previously mentioned was brought to Crime Branch Head-
quarters (C.l.) for interrogation and C.D.C. 211 and
a member of the Gendarmerie left at Lane 400/4 Peking
Road to await the arrival of an accountant Dai Lee
Tsaung (履莊) employed by the Lee Sung (立成)
Customs Brokers who have an office in the house. He
was alleged to have knowledge of the two wanted males.

At 9.30 a.m. the accountant Dai Lee Tsaung,
55, Canton, M/Accountant residing Lane 157/80 Wenchow
Road and Yang Zai (楊才), 23, Tsungming, S/Student
residing Lane 400/4 Peking Road, entered the house
and were brought to C.B.H.Q. (C.l.).

After verification of statements made and
visits to the homes of Dai Lee Tsaung and Yang Zai
being paid but nothing whatever of an incriminating
nature being found, the Gendarmerie requested that

1) Dai Lee Tsaung          (譚履莊)
   C.l. Number 210/41

下午2时45分，向片冈少尉提供了进一步协助。被告已承认
约定于下午3时左右在静安寺路大光明电影院入口处
与一名名为Gee的同伙会面。

上述警务人员提供了协助，并监视至下午4时，但结果一无所获，
遂撤除监视。

西摩路捕房和美国海军陆战队总部已获知此次行动意向。
10月11日上午7时至8时30分期间再次提供协助，当时在霞飞路（Fu Ya Ching Road，即今淮海中路）大都会戏院外
进行了监视。这也证明一无所获。

〔此处转录不清〕

1941年10月11日

Further to:-Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

On the 23-10-41 shankenko No. 974/41 was received from Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters requesting the immediate handing over of the two prisoners:-
Lee Wu Sung (李樹声) and
Lee Tsu Sz (李曹氏)

According to above Shankenko it is alleged that both the above named persons joined the "Blue Shirt Society" in January 1941 and each were receiving $70.00 monthly for allowing their residence to be used as a rendezvous for the members of a certain group of the above organisation.

As previously mentioned in diary No. 2 both these prisoners denied these allegations, as result of which the Japanese Gendarmerie were requested to supply copies of the statements made to them by these accused.

On the 24-10-41 a copy of the statement (attached) as made by the female Lee Tsu Sz was produced, but not that of the male, it being explained that he had made no statement.

The female when questioned by the S.M.Police, made a somewhat similar statement (attached) but denied that she had ever implicated her husband, in her statement to the Gendarmerie.

（左侧手写批注：S.I / B.L / 28.10 M）

如日记2中前述，这两名囚犯均否认这些指控，因此已要求日本宪兵队

1941年10月24日，提交了女囚李曹氏所作陈述的副本（附后），

该女子在接受上海公共租界工部局警务处讯问时，作了大致相似的陈述（附后），

pages.en:
Lee Su Sung (李樹声)
Chinkiang                                  // D.S.T. Lee shu Fah
Police hospital        25-10-41

My name is Lee Su Sung, age 57, native of Chinkiang,
M/Unemployed hawker, residing House 11, Lane 35 Sinza Road.
I was born in Chinkiang and since boyhood worked on
the farm of my father until the age of 38. I then came to
Shanghai and worked as a coolie in a coal hong in Hongkew for
three years. From then until 1932 I sold cigarettes and candies
on a ship plying between Shanghai and Hankow.
Following the local hostilities in 1932, I set up a
cigarette stall in Hongkew, removing to Sinza Road upon the
outbreak of hostilities in 1937.
In January this year I joined the Lai An Gambling
Den in Chapei as assistant but lost the job when the den was
closed in August. Since then I have been selling cigarettes and
candies on a ship plying between Shanghai and Chungming. This ship
was damaged in a collision in the latter part of September,
so I am now idle.
On the early morning of 16/10/41 I was arrested by
the Police at my home and handed over to the Japanese
Gendarmerie. At the Gendarmerie H.Q. I was questioned on three
occasions, viz, morning of October 16, morning of October 18
or 19, and afternoon of October 18 or 19. On all these occasions
I was questioned by two Japanese with the assistance of a
Chinese interpreter, and on the last two occasions I was burned
in the left chest and leg with a lighted candle by one of the
Japanese, resulting in injuries necessitating **〔此处转录不清〕** present
detention in hospital. In addition I was struck on the back
with a rope and on the **〔此处转录不清〕** hand and arm with a shoe casing
pages.zh:
李树声（Lee Su Sung）
镇江                                  // D.S.T. Lee shu Fah
警务处医院        1941年10月25日

我叫李树声，57岁，籍贯镇江，
男/无业小贩，居住于新闸路35弄11号。
我出生于镇江，自幼在父亲的农场工作直至38岁。随后我来
到上海，在虹口的一家煤号当了三年苦力。从那时起直到1932年，
我在往返于上海和汉口的轮船上售卖香烟和糖果。
1932年局部战事爆发后，我在虹口摆了一个香烟摊，
1937年战事爆发后搬至新闸路。
今年一月，我在闸北的来安赌台当助手，但该赌台于八月关闭，
我也因此失业。此后我一直在往返于上海和崇明的轮船上售卖香烟和糖果。
该船在九月下旬的一次碰撞中受损，
所以我现在赋闲在家。
1941年10月16日凌晨，我被警察在家中逮捕，并移交给
日本宪兵队。在宪兵队总部，我共接受了三次讯问，即10月16日上午、
10月18日或19日上午，以及10月18日或19日下午。在所有这些场合，
均由两名日本人在一名中文翻译的协助下对我进行讯问，
在后两次讯问中，其中一名日本人用点燃的蜡烛烫伤了我的
左胸和腿部，造成的伤害需要 **〔此处转录不清〕** 目前
在医院羁押。此外，我还被用绳子抽打背部，并用鞋套击打 **〔此处转录不清〕** 手和手臂

pages.en:
- 2 -

bruises.

Regarding my arrest, I am not only innocent but have
no knowledge of any political activities of any other people.
Therefore, when the Japanese Gendarmerie questioned me I could
give no useful information at all. One of the persons named
Lieu Yah Tsoong now/the son-in-law of the sister of my deceased
first wife, but I have only met this man once when he paid a
call on me at the last Chinese New Year, and I know nothing
about his doings. My present wife I married in October 1940
and she has never been concerned in political affair to my
knowledge.

Signed:
pages.zh:
- 2 -

造成淤伤。

关于我的被捕，我不仅无辜，而且对
任何其他人的政治活动一无所知。
因此，当日本宪兵队讯问我时，我完全无法
提供任何有用信息。有一个名叫刘亚忠（Lieu Yah Tsoong，音译）的人，
是我已故发妻之妹夫的姐夫（注：原文关系描述较复杂，直译为“已故第一任妻子姐妹的女婿”或类似亲属关系，此处依原文逻辑翻译为姻亲），
但我仅在去年春节他拜访我时见过此人一次，
我对他的行为一无所知。我现在的妻子是1940年10月娶的，
据我所知，她从未卷入政治事务。

签名：

pages.en:
Lee Zau Sz
as XX Japanese Gendarmerie

Lee Zau Sz (李趙氏), age 48, wife of Lee Su Sung
(李樹声), Dealer in sugar and tobacco, residing
at No. 11 Oong Ziang Li (紅祥里), Sinsa Road.

The above-mentioned person made the following
voluntary statement to the undersigned through the interpreta-
tion of K. Kawamoto on the 18-10-41 at this Gendarmerie
Detachment.
1. Not educated. No previous conviction.
1. Was married to the present husband in September last year
and the family consists of the couple only. The husband was
formerly employed as a cashier at Nanyang (南洋) Gambling
Den, address unknown, but quitted the work about two months
ago and he is at present dealing in sugar and tobacco. He
goes out of the house early in the morning and comes back late
in the evening.
.1. I will hereafter state as to my connection with one Lieu
Vung Tseong (刘文忠) and his friends.
Lieu Vung Tseong is nephew of my husband's former wife
and is said to live in Yangtseepoo District but I don't know
exactly where he lives. His occupation is also unknown to me.
In or about February this year, he together with his wife came
to my home. In or about March, this year, Lieu Vung Tseong
came to my home together with his friend named Tang Lih (陳立).
I don't know the address of Tang Lih. He is said to be
employed in a certain cotton mill.
He once came to my home and after asking me to wash clothes
pages.zh:
李赵氏（Lee Zau Sz）
作为 XX 日本宪兵队

李赵氏（Lee Zau Sz），48岁，李树声
（Lee Su Sung）之妻，糖烟商贩，
居住于新闸路红祥里（Oong Ziang Li）11号。

上述人员于1941年10月18日在本宪兵队分队，
通过川本（K. Kawamoto）的翻译，向签署人作出以下
自愿陈述。
1. 未受教育。无前科。
1. 去年九月与现任丈夫结婚，家庭仅由夫妇二人组成。丈夫
此前受雇于南洋（Nanyang）赌台担任收银员，地址不详，
但约两个月前离职，目前从事糖烟生意。他
清晨出门，深夜回家。
.1. 我将在下文陈述我与刘永忠（Lieu Vung Tseong，音译）及其朋友的关系。
刘永忠是我丈夫前妻的侄子，据说住在杨树浦区，但我不知道
他确切住在哪里。我也不知他的职业。
今年二月左右，他和他的妻子来到我家。今年三月左右，刘永忠
和他的朋友陈立（Tang Lih，音译）一起来到我家。
我不知道陈立的地址。据说他在某家棉纺厂工作。
他曾来过我家，在让我洗衣服之后

pages.en:
- 2 -

for him went back.

1. At about 4 p.m. on an unremembered date in June this
year Zung Lih and Lieu Vung Tsoong came to my home and
Zung Lih, saying that search of person is very strict, asked
me to keep a newspaper parcel which contained two pistols,
6 inches or so in length and placed it underneath a desk
in my home. I entertained suspicion about the fact that a
man who is said to be a cotton mill worker brought in pistols,
and also becoming afraid, I did not touch the parcel.

At about 10 p.m. that night, I told the fact to my
husband when he scolded me seriously and he ordered me to
return it immediately as it was a life risking danger to keep
it. At about 6 a.m. next morning Zung Lih and Lieu Vung
Tsoong came and took the pistols away.

1. Excluding Zung Lih, those friends of Lieu Vung Tsoong
who frequented my home are as follows :-

Lau Ng (老五), age about 22, residing on Robison Road
near Ferry Road. Exact address unknown.

Siao Loong (小龍), age about 22, address unknown.

Lieu Chi Wing (刘建民), age about 22, address unknown.

Mr. Chiang (蒋), age about 25, address unknown.

Mr. Chiang always accompanied Zung Lih. The above said
persons were all said to be workers of a certain cotton mill
in Yangtseepoo District. .

I. As I was distressed in maintaining my livelihood, I had
been washing clothes for them by getting $1.00 - $2.00 from
them.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

为他回去了。

1. 在今年六月某日（具体日期已记不清）下午4时许，Zung Lih 和 Lieu Vung Tsoong 来到我家。Zung Lih 称人身搜查非常严格，请求我代为保管一个报纸包裹，内有两支长约6英寸的手枪，并将其放置在我家的一张书桌底下。我对一名据称是棉纺厂工人的人携带手枪一事心生怀疑，加之心中恐惧，我便未触碰该包裹。

当晚10时许，我将此事告知丈夫，他严厉斥责了我，并命令我立即归还，因为保管此物有生命危险。次日早晨6时许，Zung Lih 和 Lieu Vung Tsoong 前来取走了手枪。

1. 除 Zung Lih 外，常来我家的 Lieu Vung Tsoong 的朋友如下：

Lau Ng (老五)，年龄约22岁，住于罗宾森路（Robison Road）靠近渡口路（Ferry Road）处。确切地址不详。

Siao Loong (小龍)，年龄约22岁，地址不详。

Lieu Chi Wing (刘建民)，年龄约22岁，地址不详。

蒋先生 (Mr. Chiang)，年龄约25岁，地址不详。

蒋先生总是陪同 Zung Lih。上述人员均称是杨树浦地区某棉纺厂的工人。

I. 由于生计艰难，我曾通过为他们洗衣赚取1.00至2.00美元。

pages.en:
- 3 -

When I was scolded and struck by my husband for
keeping the pistols, he also ordered me to stop washing
clothes for them. So I told this effect to Mr. Zung when he
said to me to meet him thereafter in front of the Sun Co.,
Nanking Road, as he would ask the washing of clothes there.

During the two months of lunar June, I met with Mr.
Zung at the said place for three or four times and was asked
by him to deliver letters to Lau Ng for three times but I did
not know the contents of the letters. Being trusted by Mr.
Zung, I did this work for him and was getting $30.00 monthly.

When he came to my home, he used to stay for a while
only and he encountered my husband several times but my
husband did not talk much in friendly manner. After the case
of pistols, he never came to my home. About a month and a
half ago, Lieu Vung Tsoong's wife came to my home and informed
me that Lieu Vung Tsoong and Mr. Zung had been arrested by
Japanese Gendarmes at his home in Yangtsepoo. I thought that
they should have been arrested by doing some evil doings as I
knew about the pistols. Although I asked Mr. Zung and others
several times what occupation were they doing but they always
replied that they all were cotton workers. I don't know at
all what work was Mr. Zung doing. The works which Mr. Zung
asked me to do were all my private job and I undertook the
works, not well knowing the nature of the works as Mr. Zung
did not tell me in details.

Mr. Zung and Lieu Vung Tsoong never came to my home
after I heard that they were arrested by the Japanese Gendarmes.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

当我因保管手枪而遭到丈夫责骂和殴打时，他也命令我停止为他们洗衣。于是我将此意告知 Zung 先生，他随后告诉我，以后在南京路先施公司（Sun Co.）门前与他见面，因为他会在那里委托洗衣事宜。

在农历六月的两个月期间，我在上述地点与 Zung 先生会面三四次，并受他之托三次向 Lau Ng 送信，但我不知信件内容。出于对 Zung 先生的信任，我替他做了这项工作，每月获得30.00美元。

当他来我家时，通常只停留片刻，他曾几次遇到我丈夫，但我丈夫并未与其友好多谈。在手枪事件之后，他再未来过我家。大约一个半月前，Lieu Vung Tsoong 的妻子来到我家，告知我 Lieu Vung Tsoong 和 Zung 先生已在杨树浦的家中被日本宪兵逮捕。鉴于我知道手枪之事，我想他们定是因做了坏事而被捕。虽然我多次询问 Zung 先生等人从事何种职业，但他们总是回答都是棉纺工人。我完全不知道 Zung 先生究竟做什么工作。Zung 先生让我做的工作都属于我的私活，由于 Zung 先生未详细说明，我在不太了解工作性质的情况下承接了这些工作。

在我听说他们被日本宪兵逮捕后，Zung 先生和 Lieu Vung Tsoong 再未来过我家。

pages.en:
- 4 -

I met with Mr. Zung seven or eight times at my home
and three or four times in front of the Sun Co. Lau Ng came
to my home four or five times. I paid a visit at his (Lau
Ng's) home three times. Siau Loong came to my home
accompanying Zung Lih five or six times. Siao Loong came to
my home about half a month ago, but he never put in an
appearance since. Chiang came to my home accompanying Mr.
Zung five or six times but I have not seen him these one
month. Liou Chi Ming came to my home over ten times.
1. As stated above, I don't know with what group Mr. Zung
and others had connection or what works were they doing.
I did the work, not well knowing the nature of their
works.

Statement taken by :- Sgt. Major
Kunitada Mukoyama.
-----------------------

2ND STATEMENT

1. Zung Lih alias Dien Jih stayed at my home for about one
month in or about April this year.
Because he had no family to nurse whilst his being
confined to bed, suffering from fever, I attended him during
the time.
The time when Lieu Vung Tseong and his friends began to
come to my home is January or the beginning of February of
this year, I think. My husband also knows them because he met
them too. In the meantime, I understood that my home is being
used as a rendezvous for them but I did not know what matters
pages.zh:
- 4 -

我在家中与 Zung 先生见过七八次，在先施公司门前见过三四次。Lau Ng 来过我家四五次。我去过他家（Lau Ng 的家）三次。Siau Loong 陪同 Zung Lih 来过我家五六次。Siao Loong 约半个月前曾来过我家，但此后未曾露面。Chiang 陪同 Zung 先生来过我家五六次，但这一个月来我没见过他。Liou Chi Ming 来过我家十多次。
1. 如上所述，我不知道 Zung 先生等人与哪个团体有联系，也不知道他们在做什么工作。我在不太了解其工作性质的情况下做了这些工作。

记录人：军曹
Kunitada Mukoyama（音译）。
---

第二次供词

1. Zung Lih，别名 Dien Jih，于今年四月左右在我家住了约一个月。
因他患病发烧卧床期间无人照料，我在此期间照顾了他。
我想 Lieu Vung Tseong 及其朋友开始来我家的时间是今年一月或二月初。我丈夫也认识他们，因为他也曾见过他们。在此期间，我明白我家被用作他们的聚会地点，但我不知道他们

pages.en:
- 5 -

were they talking about.
Squad chief and five or six others met for five or
six times and this my husband also knows. During their
meeting we used to go out and the time of meeting was less
than one hour. One or two men came at the rate of two times
a week and the meeting was held between 2 and 4 o'clock in
the afternoon. When they came in, they entered without any
greeting and sometimes spent times by drinking tea freely.
1. The persons whom I know are the Squad Chief, a plump
fellow, name unknown, Zung Lih, Lieu Vung Tsoong, Lieu Chi
Ming, Siau Lieu, Mr. Chiang, Lau Sai and Lau Ng, eight in
number. The money was given by Zung Lih and since March or
April I got $30.00 to $60.00 per month but after Zung Lih was
arrested I have not obtained any money. My husband knows
about the money, as I had been washing clothes for them. My
husband talked with them sometimes, but I cannot say whether
he had any detailed knowledge about them.
1. The letters Zung Lih trusted me were packed in white
papers and I took the letters to Lau Ng's home and handed same
directly to him and brought back letters of answer and handed
same to Zung Lih when he came to my home. As I have not told
my husband about the letters, I think he has no knowledge
about them. It is true that Lieu Vung Tsoong's friends had a
meeting, but I don't know the subject of their conversations.

Statement taken by:- Sgt. Major K. Nakayama
on the 20-10-41.
pages.zh:
- 5 -

谈论的是什么事情。
班长及其他五六人聚会了五六次，我丈夫也知道此事。在他们聚会期间，我们通常会外出，聚会时间少于一小时。有一两个人每周来两次，聚会时间在下午2点至4点之间。他们进来时不打招呼，有时随意喝茶消磨时间。
1. 我认识的人有：班长（一名胖男子，姓名不详）、Zung Lih、Lieu Vung Tsoong、Lieu Chi Ming、Siau Lieu、蒋先生、Lau Sai 和 Lau Ng，共八人。钱款由 Zung Lih 支付，自三月或四月起，我每月得到30.00至60.00美元，但在 Zung Lih 被捕后，我再未收到任何钱款。我丈夫知道这笔钱的事，因为我一直在为他们洗衣。我丈夫有时与他们交谈，但我无法说他是否对他们有详细了解。
1. Zung Lih 托付给我的信件用白纸包着，我将信送到 Lau Ng 家中直接交给他，并带回回信，在 Zung Lih 来我家时交给他。由于我未将信件之事告诉丈夫，我想他对此并不知情。Lieu Vung Tsoong 的朋友们确实开过会，但我不知道他们谈话的主题。

记录人：军曹 K. Nakayama（音译）
于1941年10月20日。

pages.en:
Lee Zau Sz (李曹氏)
Pootung // D.I. Crighton
C.B.H.Q. 24-10-41 D.S.I. Zia Vai Faing

My name is Lee Zau Sz. I am 48 years old a native of
Pootung, wife of Lee Su Sung (李樹声).
I was married to my present husband in September
1940, and we live alone having no children.
Previously my husband was employed in the Nanyang
Gambling den, Chapei but two months ago he left this job and
became a dealer in tobacco and confectionary. Usually my
husband left home early in the morning and did not return until
late at night, therefore most of the time I was at home by
myself.
One day in January 1941 a male and female Chinese
visited our home and I was introduced to the former whose name
was Lieu Vung Tsoong (刘文忠) a nephew of my husband's
first wife. At that time I was given to understand that both
were living in the Yangtszepoo area, but the exact location
I never found out, also I did not know his occupation although
I had heard that he worked in some cotton mill.
Sometime in March 1941 Lieu Vung Tsoong again called
at my home, during my husband's absence and on this occasion
he brought with him a friend named Zung Lih (陳立) whom he
introduced to me. I understand that the latter was also employ-
ed in a cotton mill but where I don't know. At this time Zung
Lih asked me whether or not I would do his washing for him, he
would pay me for same. Owing to our poor financial standing,
my husband earning very little money, I accepted his proposal
and from this time on I used to wash clothes for him at least
three times a week and he used to pay me $30.00 per month.
pages.zh:
Lee Zau Sz (李曹氏)
浦东 // D.I. Crighton（音译）
中央捕房总部 1941年10月24日 D.S.I. Zia Vai Faing（音译）

我叫 Lee Zau Sz。现年48岁，浦东人，系 Lee Su Sung (李樹声) 之妻。
我于1940年9月与现任丈夫结婚，我们独自生活，无子女。
此前，我丈夫受雇于闸北南洋赌窟，但两个月前他辞去了这份工作，成为烟草和糖果经销商。通常我丈夫清晨离家，深夜方归，因此大部分时间我独自在家。
1941年1月的一天，一男一女两名中国人来访，我被介绍给那名男子，他叫 Lieu Vung Tsoong (刘文忠)，是我丈夫原配的侄子。当时我得知他们都住在杨树浦地区，但我从未查明确切地点，也不知道他的职业，虽然听说他在某家棉纺厂工作。
1941年3月的某天，Lieu Vung Tsoong 再次趁我丈夫不在时来访，这次他带来了一位名叫 Zung Lih (陳立) 的朋友，并介绍给我。我得知后者也受雇于一家棉纺厂，但不知具体地点。当时 Zung Lih 问我是否愿意为他洗衣，他会支付报酬。由于家境贫寒，丈夫收入微薄，我接受了他的提议，从此我每周至少为他洗衣三次，他每月支付我30.00美元。

pages.en:
- 2 -

Between March and June 1941 Lieu Vung Tsoong and Zung
Lih used to visit me quite frequently and occasionally they
would bring friends with them. Amongst the latter I can
remember the following:-

1. Lau Ng (老五) age about 22, residing somewhere
On Robison Road.
2. Siao Lieu (小刘) age 22, address unknown.
3. Lieu Chi Ming (刘建民) age 24, address unknown.
4. Mr. Chiang (蒋) age 25, address unknown.

Mr. Chiang after a time used always to accompany Zung Lih.
Occasionally those persons used all to meet in my home
during the afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. but what they
discussed I don't know as I used to be asked to leave the room.
On one or two occasions my husband would be present in
home when those people arrived, but beyond holding brief
casual conversations with them he never took part in their
discussions and if anything used to disprove of them coming
there.

One afternoon at about 4 p.m. during the month of June
1941 Lieu Vung Tsoong and Zung Lih came to my home, during
my husband's absence, and at this time I Zung Lih take two
black objects from under his long gown and wrap them in a
piece of paper, after which he placed the package under a
desk in the room. I enquired of him what it was, but he did
not tell me merely stating that as there was a Police Search
Party operating outside he wished to leave the package there
temporary. As I had identified the black objects as pistols,
pages.zh:
- 2 -

1941年3月至6月间，Lieu Vung Tsoong 和 Zung Lih 经常来访，偶尔会带朋友同行。其中我能记得的有以下人员：

1. Lau Ng (老五)，年龄约22岁，住在罗宾森路（Robison Road）某处。
2. Siao Lieu (小刘)，年龄22岁，地址不详。
3. Lieu Chi Ming (刘建民)，年龄24岁，地址不详。
4. 蒋先生 (Mr. Chiang)，年龄25岁，地址不详。

过了一段时间，蒋先生总是陪同 Zung Lih。
偶尔这些人会在下午2点至4点之间在我家聚会，但我不知道他们讨论什么，因为我常被要求离开房间。
有一两次，当这些人到达时，我丈夫在家，但他除了与他们进行简短的寒暄外，从未参与他们的讨论，甚至对他们的到来表示不悦。

1941年6月的一个下午，约4时许，Lieu Vung Tsoong 和 Zung Lih 趁我丈夫不在时来到我家。当时我看见 Zung Lih 从长袍下取出两个黑色物体，用一张纸包好，然后将包裹放在房间的书桌底下。我问他是什么，他没有告诉我，只是说外面有警察搜查队行动，他想暂时将包裹留在那里。由于我认出那些黑色物体是手枪，

pages.en:
- 3 -

I became afraid and that evening when my husband returned I
explained to him what had happened. He became very angry and
in addition to beating me, told me I was a fool in asmuch as
that it would be a case of life and death if such things were
found in our home. He then ordered me to immediately remove
them from the room and also informed me that in future none
of those persons must visit our home. I explained that Zung
Lih had promised to call back for the package and as it would
be dangerous for me to carry the parcel. We had better leave
it until the following day.

At about 6 a.m. the next day Zung Lin and Lieu Vang
Tsoong came and removed the parcel whilst my husband was still
asleep and at this time I told Zung about the beating I had
received and also that my husband had forbidden them the
future use of our home.

Zung Lin then arranged that I meet him that afternoon
at between 3 and 4 p.m. outside the Sun Company, Nanking Rd.
Without the knowledge of my husband I kept this
appointment and from this time on we met two or three times
some place.

About this time Zung asked me to deliver certain
letters to the home of one Lau Ng at Ying Hwa Li, Robison Rd.
and during the months of June and July 1941 I delivered about
four or five such letters and on each occasion I brought
back a reply to Zung Lih who used to wait for me at the same
place by appointment. For this service I received no
financial benefit.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

我感到害怕，当晚丈夫回来后，我向他解释了发生的事。他非常生气，除了打我之外，还说我真是个傻瓜，因为如果家里被发现藏有此类物品，将是生死攸关的大事。随后他命令我立即将它们移出房间，并告知我今后不许这些人再来我家。我解释说 Zung Lih 承诺会回来取走包裹，且由我携带包裹会有危险，我们最好留到第二天再说。

次日早晨6时许，Zung Lin 和 Lieu Vang Tsoong 前来取走包裹，当时我丈夫仍在熟睡。此时我告诉 Zung 我挨打的事，以及我丈夫禁止他们今后使用我家作为聚会地点。

Zung Lin 随即安排我当天下午3点至4点之间在南京路先施公司外与他见面。
我在丈夫不知情的情况下赴约，从此我们在某个地方又见面了两三次。

大约在此时，Zung 让我送几封信到罗宾森路英华里（Ying Hwa Li）一位名叫 Lau Ng 的人家中。在1941年6月和7月期间，我送了大约四五封这样的信，每次我都带回一封回信交给 Zung Lih，他按约定在同一地点等我。为此服务，我没有获得任何经济利益。

pages.en:
About the end of August or the beginning of Sept.
1941 the wife of Lieu Vung Tsoong came to my home and inform-
ed me that Lieu and Zung Lin had been arrested by the
Japanese Gendarmerie at their home in Yangtzepoo, and
regarding the pistols I was not surprised, but I did not
inform my husband.

Since the arrest of those two men I have seen nothing
of the others.

Although I enquired of Zung several times what work
he was doing he would never tell me.

After I began delivering letters for Mr. Zung, he
increased my washing money to $60.00 per month, however after
two or three months this ceased and since the arrest of these
persons I have received nothing.

Question:- In your statement to the Japanese Gendarmerie you
stated that your husband knew of all your connect-
ions with these persons, also that on several
occasions he held long discussion with them.

Answer:- My husband has absolutely nothing to do with these
people and the Japanese interpreter must have
misunderstood me, as I cannot recollect having
said anything such as they mention.

Signed:
pages.zh:
1941年8月底或9月初，Lieu Vung Tsoong 的妻子来到我家，告知我 Lieu 和 Zung Lin 已在杨树浦的家中被日本宪兵队逮捕。关于手枪一事，我并不感到惊讶，但我没有告诉丈夫。

自从这两人被捕后，我再未见过其他人。

虽然我多次询问 Zung 他做什么工作，但他从不告诉我。

在我开始为 Zung 先生送信后，他将我的洗衣费增加到每月60.00美元，然而两三个月后这一待遇停止，自这些人被捕以来，我再未收到任何款项。

问：你在向日本宪兵队的供词中称，你丈夫知道你与这些人的所有往来，并且曾多次与他们进行长时间讨论。

答：我丈夫与这些人毫无关系，日本翻译一定误解了我的意思，因为我不记得说过他们提到的那些话。

签名：

pages.en:
C.l.Misc.214 41
Headquarters
Crime Branch
October 24th
41
2

Further to : Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

On the 23-10-41 the prisoners Lee Su Sung
(李樹声) and Lee Zau Sz (李曹义) were returned to Crime
Branch Headquarters along with a written request for
their permanent handing over on the grounds that they
had admitted being concerned in anti-Japanese activities.

Both were later questioned regarding their
admission to the Japanese Gendarmerie, but denied that
they had made any written statements admitting the
allegations made against them.

In view of this and in order to facilitate
further investigations a request was made to the Gendar-
merie that copies of the statements as made by those two
prisoners be loaned to Crime Branch Headquarters.

On the morning of October 24, 1941, the prisoner
Lee Su Sung reported sick and requested medical attention.

He was sent to the Police Hospital where he was
detained, his medical certificate reading;

"Burns of leg and chest detained, requires
ten days treatment."

Questioned as to how he came by his injuries
he stated that same had been inflicted upon him during
his detention at Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters.

（左侧手写批注：5! / gl / 2H 10 H）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / OCT 24 1941 / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（左下角手写批注及方框印章：〔此处转录不清〕）
（右下角签名：John Coghlan）
pages.zh:
C.l.Misc.214 41
总部
刑事科
10月24日
41
2

续：协助日本宪兵队

1941年10月23日，囚犯李樹声（Lee Su Sung）和李曹义（Lee Zau Sz）被送回刑事科总部，并附有一份书面请求，要求将他们永久移交，理由是他们承认参与了反日活动。

随后，两人就向日本宪兵队所作的供述接受了讯问，但否认曾作出任何书面陈述以承认针对他们的指控。

鉴于此，并为便于进一步调查，已向宪兵队提出请求，希望借阅这两名囚犯所作陈述的副本至刑事科总部。

1941年10月24日上午，囚犯李樹声报称患病并请求就医。

他被送往警察医院并被拘留，其医疗证明写明：

“腿部及胸部烧伤，需治疗十天。”

当被问及如何受伤时，他称这些伤是在日本宪兵队总部被拘留期间遭受的。

（左侧手写批注：5! / gl / 2H 10 H）
（左侧印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1941年10月24日 / 特务科）
（左下角手写批注及方框印章：〔此处转录不清〕）
（右下角签名：John Coghlan）

pages.en:
D. C. (Special Branch).

C.l. Misc.314/41

MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
D.8299/334
16 10 41

Headquarters
Crime Branch
16th October 41.

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 12.30 a.m. 16-10-41 Sergeant Major Ikeda accompanied by other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie and a Chinese informer, came to Crime Branch Headquarters C.l. and requested assistance to visit House No. 11, Lane 35, Sinza Road, for purpose of, if possible, effecting the arrest of one named Lee (李) said to be a prominent member of the "Blue Shirts Society".

Necessary arrangements having been made with the U.S. Marine Corp and Sinza Station the desired assistance was rendered by D.I. Crighton D.S. Yamahara, D.S. I. Zia Vai Faung, C.D. C.s 40 and 252.

On arrival at the address in question the wanted man was pointed out by the informer and on being questioned gave his particulars etc as follows:-

1. Lee Su Sung(李樹声) age 54, native of Chinkiang, M/Unemployed, previously employed as a guard at the Lai An ( ) Gambling House, Lai An Li( ), Paoshan Road, Chapel.

At this stage Sergeant Major Ikeda requested that the wanted man's wife:-

2. Lee Kau Su(李曹氏) age 48, native of Shanghai, M/Female,
be taken to Crime Branch H.Q. for questioning.

A search of the room occupied by these two persons revealed nothing of an incriminating nature.

（左侧手写批注：5.1 / 16.10 H1）
（左侧印章：SPECIAL BRANCH）
（左侧手写批注：by b.c / help.o / P 1/10）
pages.zh:
D. C. (特务科)。

C.l. Misc.314/41

公共租界警务处
档案室
D.8299/334
1941年10月16日

总部
刑事科
1941年10月16日

1

协助日本宪兵队

1941年10月16日凌晨12时30分，池田（Ikeda）警曹长在其他日本宪兵队员和一名中国线人的陪同下，来到刑事科总部（C.l.），请求协助前往新闸路35弄11号，目的是尽可能逮捕一名姓李（Lee）的男子，据称此人是“蓝衣社”的重要成员。

在与美国海军陆战队及新闸捕房作出必要安排后，由督察克里顿（Crighton）、副督察山原（Yamahara）、副督察谢伟芳（I. Zia Vai Faung，音译）以及华捕40号和252号提供了所需的协助。

到达上述地址后，线人指认了被通缉者，经讯问，其个人资料等如下：-

1. 李樹声（Lee Su Sung），54岁，镇江籍，男/无业，此前曾在闸北宝山路来安里（Lai An Li）来安（Lai An）赌场担任看守。

此时，池田警曹长要求将被通缉者的妻子：-

2. 李曹氏（Lee Kau Su），48岁，上海籍，女，
带往刑事科总部接受讯问。

对这两人所住房间的搜查未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

pages.en:
Tseng Yong **〔此处转录不清〕** (張雲程) also 22 years Tsung Bang (許鵬)
Tientsin // O.J.I. Lee Shu Fah
C.R.H.Q. 27-10-41

I was born in Shanghai in 1920. Between the ages of 8
and 17 years I studied in various primary schools. In February
1936 I went to study in the Dan Kung Middle School, 131 Hankow
Road, and was graduated in June 1941. I used to live in the
school dormitory and owing to the fact that I had no home in
Shanghai I continued to live there after my graduation.
In October 1940, through the introduction of another
student name Fu You Sung (傅友生), (now in custody of
Japanese Gendarmerie), I became a member of the Three People's
Young Men's Corps. In October and November 1940 I distributed
Anti-Japanese handbills on about five different occasions, i.e.,
once from the Sun Co. Roof Garden, twice from tramcars. I
don't remember how I distributed the handbills on the other
occasions.
I have not been concerned in any other Anti-Japanese
activities.

Signed:

**〔此处转录不清〕**
pages.zh:
曾永**〔此处转录不清〕**（张云程），另有一名22岁的许鹏（Tsung Bang，音译）
天津 // O.J.I. 李树法（Lee Shu Fah，音译）
中央巡捕房总部 1941年10月27日

我于1920年出生在上海。8至17岁期间，我在多所小学就读。1936年2月，我进入汉口路131号的大公中学学习，并于1941年6月毕业。我过去住在学校宿舍，由于我在上海没有家，毕业后继续住在那里。
1940年10月，通过另一名学生傅友生（Fu You Sung，现由日本宪兵队羁押）的介绍，我成为了三民主义青年团团员。1940年10月和11月，我大约五次分发反日传单，即一次在新新公司屋顶花园，两次在有轨电车上。我不记得其他几次是如何分发传单的。
我没有参与其他任何反日活动。

Men's Corps

The arrested man Tsang Yoong Zung (程雲程) alias
Tsang Bang (張朋) was loaned to the Gendarmerie for one
week, against receipt, on the morning of 17-10-41.

At 4 p.m. Sergeant Major Yoshino attended Crime
Branch Headquarters (C.l.) together with the male and
stated he had admitted being a member of the Three
Peoples Principles Young Men's Corps and that another
student at the Dah Koong (大公) Middle School 131 Hankow
Road was also a member. They wished to effect his arrest.

Assistance rendered by D.S. Yoshinaga, D.S.I.
Yang Shih Kwang, C.D.S. 69 and the undersigned at 4.15 p.m.
but the wanted man Chiang Ping En(蔣秉恩) was not
located. It was learned he had not appeared in class during
the morning and had apparently left the premises after the
arrest of Tsang Yoong Zung.

Several patriotic posters along corridors were
removed at the request of the Gendarmerie.

Central Station informed of the visit.

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 6 a.m. on the 17th October 1941, Sergeant
Yoshino and two other members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie called at H.Q.C.B. (C.I.) Offices and
requested assistance to visit dormitory of the Dah
Koong (大公) Middle School at 131 Hankow Road to arrest
a former student of this school one named Tsang Yoong
Zung (張雲程), who, according to the Gendarmes, is a
member of the Three Peoples Principles Young Men's Corps
engaged in anti-Japanese activities.

The necessary assistance was rendered by D.S.I.
Lee Shu Fa, D.S. Sugimoto, C.D.S. 40 and the undersigned.
The school in question was visited at 6.30 a.m. and the
wanted man arrested. His particulars are as follows :-

Tsang Yoong Zung (張雲程) alias Tsang Pang
(張), age 22, native of
Tientsin, s/Unemployed, N.P.A.
(C.I. Prisoner No. 232/41).

Nothing of an incriminating nature has been found
in his personal effects.

Upon being questioned, he denied being a member
of the Three Peoples Principles Young Men's Corps or
having ever been engaged in any anti-Japanese activities.

（左侧手写批注：B.L. 10/10）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 17 OCT 1941）

Prior to leaving this address Sergeant Major
Ikeda requested permission to leave one of his men for
purpose of maintaining a watch as it was suspected that
other members of the same organisation might visit same.
This was granted C.D.C. 252 and one member of the Gendar-
merie remaining behind.

On return to Crime Branch Headquarters both pri-
soners were subject to a lengthy interrogation, but
denied the allegations made against them, as result of
which Sergeant Major Ikeda requested their handing over
on loan.

Both prisoners were handed over on loan for
a period of one week against the usual receipt (attached).

At 4.30 a.m. 16-10-41 Sergeant Major Ikeda
requested a further assistance to visit a certain house
located in the Ying Hwa Li, Robison Road, for purpose of
if possible effecting the arrest of one named Yang(楊),
the information on this occasion being supplied by the arrest-
ed female Lee Han Sz.

Arrangments having been made with the U.S.
（批：16 10 AM）Marine Corp and Pootoo Road Station the desired assistance
was given, however on arrival at the address in question,
i.e. House 1106 Ying Hwa Li, Robison Road, it was
ascertained that the wanted man had gone to Soochow one
month ago.

John Caphans
pages.zh:
1/2

在离开该地址之前，池田（Ikeda）警曹长请求允许留下一名手下进行监视，因为怀疑该组织的其他成员可能会来访。此请求获准，由华捕252号和一名宪兵队员留下看守。

回到刑事科总部后，两名囚犯接受了长时间的讯问，但否认了对他们的指控，因此池田警曹长请求将他们借出。

两名囚犯均按惯例出具收据（附后）被借出，为期一周。

1941年10月16日凌晨4时30分，池田警曹长请求再次提供协助，前往罗别根路（Robison Road）英华里（Ying Hwa Li）的一处房屋，目的是尽可能逮捕一名姓杨（Yang）的男子，此次情报由被捕女子李韩氏（Lee Han Sz，音译）提供。

在与美国
（批：10月16日上午）海军陆战队及普陀路捕房作出安排后，提供了所需的协助，然而到达上述地址，即罗别根路英华里1106号时，查明被通缉者已于一个月前前往苏州。

John Caphans

Further to : Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie re
goods allegedly destined for the Chungking Government

Regarding the property mentioned in diary 1,
it was learned on the morning of October 20, 1941, that
the man in custody of the Gendarmerie Wong Yeu Tsong
(王以莊) had come to an amicable agreement with the
management of the Chekiang Provincial Bank whereby
they would allow the goods stored in their godown to
be taken away by him, against receipt, without the
production of the godown warrants which are alleged to
be in possession of one of the not-arrested men.

The goods were removed by Wong Yeu Tsong on
the morning of 20-10-41. A copy of the receipt signed
by him is attached to the main file.

Reference the transmitting sets and parts stored
in the godown of Marden's at 117 Nanking Road, Mr. Hyl
Fah Yue (悅化玉) Manager of Amateurs Home, 323 Kiangsu
Road, procured a new delivery order from Marden's. With
the production of this and the godown warrant, both
chopped by Wong Yeu Tsong, Marden's will release the
goods stored by them to Wong Yeu Tsong.

In view of the arrangements agreed upon, further
action by the S.M.Police was not considered necessary
and the Japanese Headquarters were informed to this effect.

关于据称运往重庆政府的货物

关于日记1中提到的财产，1941年10月20日上午获悉，由宪兵队羁押的王以莊（Wong Yeu Tsong）已与浙江省银行管理层达成友好协议，允许他将存放在该行仓库中的货物提走，只需出具收据，无需出示据称由一名未被捕男子持有的仓单。

货物已于1941年10月20日上午由王以莊运走。由其签署的收据副本已附在主卷宗中。

关于存放在南京路117号马登洋行（Marden's）仓库中的发射机及零件，江苏路323号业余无线电之家（Amateurs Home）经理悦化玉（Hyl Fah Yue，音译）先生从马登洋行获取了一份新的提货单。凭借此提货单及均由王以莊盖章的仓单，马登洋行将把存放的货物释放给王以莊。

鉴于已达成上述安排，认为上海公共租界工部局警务处无需采取进一步行动，并已就此通知日本宪兵队总部。

In order to clarify the situation regarding
the five cases, I. Kobayashi and the undersigned
interviewed Mr. W.J. Hawkings of the Godown Dept. of
Marlens on the morning of October 15, 1941.

He confirmed that such a Godown Warrant had
been issued and that the goods were stored in 117
Hongkong Road. As far as Marlen's were concerned the
property was stored in the name of Amateurs Home and
unless they received definite instructions from the
British Court, the goods would be handed to Amateurs
Home against production of the Godown Warrant.

These points have been explained to the Gendar-
merie as also what steps will be necessary regarding
application to the British Court if they consider the
property is that of the Chungking Government.

The man in custody also stated other cases of
sundry goods had from time to time been purchased by
himself or one of the other men and stored in the
No.1 Godown of the Chekiang Provincial Bank at Lane
806/88 North Soochow Road. The Godown warrants regarding
these however were in the possession of one or more
of the not-arrested men.

为了澄清这五个箱子的情况，小林（I. Kobayashi）和本人于1941年10月15日上午会见了马伦斯（Marlens）仓库部的 W.J. Hawkings 先生。

他确认已签发此类仓库栈单，且货物存于香港路117号。就马伦斯方面而言，财产是以“业余者之家”的名义存储的，除非他们收到英国法院的明确指示，否则将在出示仓库栈单后将货物交给“业余者之家”。

已向宪兵队解释了这些要点，以及如果他们认为该财产属于重庆政府，在向英国法院申请时需要采取的步骤。

被拘留男子还陈述，其他一些杂项货物的箱子曾由他本人或其他人之一不时购买，并存放在北苏州路806/88弄浙江省银行第一仓库中。然而，关于这些货物的仓库栈单由一名或多名未被逮捕的男子持有。

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie
re arrest of terrorist in Nantao

At 3 p.m. October 21, 1941, Sub-Lieutenant Ikeda
of Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters attended Crime Branch
Headquarters (C.l.) with one in custody named
Zau Tsoong Tsai (趙振才) 28, Shantung
who was arrested at about 6.30 p.m. 19-10-41 in Nantao
immediately after an unsuccessful attempt by him to assass-
inate Wong Tsung Ding (王正廷).

（批：S.L. 22.10.41）

A request was made to visit Lane 21 House 8
Hupeh Road wherein the arrested male stated he had lived
for five days.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 22 OCT 1941）

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung,
D/S Sugimoto, C.D.C. 252 and the undersigned at 3.15 p.m.
when the house in question was visited but no one on the
premises recalled having seen the arrested male before.

No search was made and nothing was seized.

The arrested male maintained he had stayed there
during the period stated but nothing was learned which
would confirm this.

Luna station informed of the visit.

It is learned that the weapon seized at the time
of this man's arrest was one of those used in the murder
of H.A. IVANOV, Russian, (Changte Road F.Y.Jb 1033/41.).

（批：Basho 331°）

1941年10月21日下午3时，日本宪兵队总部的池田少尉（Sub-Lieutenant Ikeda）带着一名在押人员赵振才（Zau Tsoong Tsai），28岁，山东人，来到刑事处总部（C.l.）。此人于1941年10月19日下午6时30分左右在南市被捕，当时他企图刺杀王正廷（Wong Tsung Ding）未遂。

（批：S.L. 1941年10月22日）

提出请求访问湖北路21弄8号，被捕男子称他在那里住了五天。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处 1941年10月22日）

下午3时15分，督察长谢维方（Zia Vai Faung）、警佐杉本（Sugimoto）、刑事侦缉探员252号及本人提供了协助，访问了该房屋，但现场无人记得以前见过被捕男子。

未进行搜查，也未扣押任何物品。

被捕男子坚持称他在所述期间住在那里，但未获得任何能证实这一点的信息。

已通知卢纳电台（Luna station）此次访问。

获悉，在此人被捕时缴获的武器是用于谋杀俄国人 H.A. IVANOV 的武器之一（常德路 F.Y.Jb 1033/41案）。

（批：Basho 331°）

Mau Tsung Hwa (毛春華) alias Wong Zung (王成)
// D.S.I. Sicu Shang Tsah
translated
xxxxxx Y.C. Chang

Zangzoh
H. Q. C. B. 3-12-41

My name is Mau Tsung Hwa alias Wong Zung, age 37, native
of Hsupoo, Zangzoh Hsien, married, unemployed, and residing in
a lodging house.

Since the age of 8 years, I had studied in a private
school at my native place for six years, and became unemployed
at the age of 15 years. When I was 17 years of age, I was employed
as an accountant on a ship for six years, after which I
became a teacher at my native village. At the age of 32 years,
I was the village-headman of the Fu Tung Village near Hsupoo
City for eight months.

In October 1937 as the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke
out and the Japanese troops landed at Hsupoo, Zangzoh, I re-
moved to Yiensung, Kiangsu. In June 1938 I returned to Hsupoo, my
native place, where I was then employed as a clerk in a trans-
portation company, but after about three months I resigned
from this job owing to my quarrel with my fellow-employees.

In May or June 1938, through the introduction of one Koo
Lai Siu, being a friend of mine, I became a member of the New
4th Army stationed at Mi Lee Dong Bridge, near Hsupoo, Zangzoh,
the captain of which was one named Sung Tien Shih. In July the
same year, Sung Tien Shih despatched me to Deng Bang village,
where I was ordered to carry on transportation activities.

In January 1941 Sung Tien Shih employed me as the chief
of the military section of the New 4th Army in the villages of
Zangzoh. Later I was informed that the Japanese soldiers often
investigated the various villages of Zangzoh for arresting
Anti-Japanese members, therefore I left there and came to
pages.zh:
毛春华 (Mau Tsung Hwa) 化名王成 (Wong Zung)
// 督察长 Sicu Shang Tsah
翻译
xxxxxx Y.C. Chang

Zangzoh
刑事处总部 1941年12月3日

我叫毛春华，化名王成，37岁，籍贯江苏阜浦县（音译），已婚，无业，居住在客栈。

我从8岁起在家乡私塾读书六年，15岁时失业。17岁时，我在船上担任会计六年，之后回到家乡村庄当老师。32岁时，我曾在阜浦市附近的富东村（音译）担任村长八个月。

1937年10月，中日战事爆发，日军在江苏阜浦登陆，我搬至江苏盐城（音译）。1938年6月，我回到家乡阜浦，受雇于一家运输公司担任职员，但因与同事争吵，约三个月后辞职。

1938年5月或6月，通过我的朋友顾来孝（Koo Lai Siu，音译）的介绍，我成为驻扎在江苏阜浦附近米李东桥（Mi Lee Dong Bridge，音译）的新四军成员，该部队队长名为宋天石（Sung Tien Shih，音译）。同年7月，宋天石派我到邓邦村（Deng Bang village，音译），命令我从事运输活动。

1941年1月，宋天石任命我为新四军在江苏各村镇的军事部门主管。后来我得知，日军经常搜查江苏各村镇以逮捕抗日分子，因此我离开那里来到

pages.en:
- 2 -

Shanghai in June this year.

At about 7 a.m. on 24-10-41 I was arrested in Room 47
of the Shing Ming Lodging House, located at 203/22 Hupeh Road.
This is my true statement.

Signed:
pages.zh:
- 2 -

上海，时间是今年6月。

1941年10月24日上午7时许，我在湖北路203/22号星明客栈（Shing Ming Lodging House）47号房间被捕。
这是我的真实供词。

Headquarters

October 24, 41
2

Further to: Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

In reference to the letter seized at the
offices of Song Kyi Sung (王啟深) and claimed by the
Japanese Gendarmerie to contain subversive writings
same has now been translated by the Special Branch
and reads as follows :-

" Envelope

To Ming Kai Ming,
284 Kiukiang Road,
from Ming, Chungking. February 27.

Post marked:- Chungking 28-2-40.
Shanghai 5-3-40.

Written on reverse of envelope :-

K.P. Sorry, I have to request you to bring
my typewriter to school tomorrow morning.
Tsaung.

...............

1st Letter : (Letter written on lesson papers
of the Military Engineering School
of the Ministry of War).

To brother Tsuh Sang,

My previous letter might have reached
you. Regarding Research Institute, have you
received any letter from Ah Yuh?
We are going to have experiments on
electrical engineering in the Central
University and I have learned more particulars
regarding the Research Institute in that
University. According to a junior professor
of the university, there is only a telegraph
communication between institutes in the
university but this institute really exists
in name; its classes have just been open.

（批：5/ 8L 2H·10 H'）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE OCT 24 1941 SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：18 1/10 10/10 b.pio.）

2

关于在宋启深（Song Kyi Sung，原文与后文王啟祥名字混淆，此处依原文译）办公室查获并被日本宪兵队声称包含颠覆性内容的信件，特别支部现已将其翻译，内容如下：-

“信封

致明凯明（Ming Kai Ming），
九江路284号，
来自重庆的明（Ming）。2月27日。

邮戳：- 重庆 1940年2月28日。
上海 1940年3月5日。

写在信封背面：-

K.P. 抱歉，我不得不请你明天早上把我的打字机带到学校去。
庄____ (Tsaung ____)

第一封信：（信写在陆军部军事工程学校的练习纸上）。

致树桑（Tsuh Sang）兄：

我上一封信可能已经寄达你处。关于研究所一事，你是否收到阿玉（Ah Yuh）的来信？
我们要在中央大学进行电气工程实验，我已了解到该大学研究所的更多详情。据该校一位初级教授称，校内各研究所之间仅有电报联系，但该研究所确实名义上存在；其课程刚刚开设。

（批：5/ 8L 2H·10 H'）
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1941年10月24日 特别支部）
（批：18 1/10 10/10 b.pio.）

pages.en:
2/2

He thinks it is inadvisable to join it.
However, I do not agree with him regarding
this point. We can have plenty of experiments
in the institute and can use a library to
increase our knowledge, and possibly we can
get a degree later on. I therefore hope you
will be determined to join a research institute.
I expect there will be an Electric Power
Research Institute in the Joint University in
the South-East, and wish that Ah Poh will not
stop you.
    I feel that my knowledge is very limited.
My school days become shorter and shorter but
there is very much for me to learn yet. I am
now anxious to have laboratory experiments so
that I can be useful.
    You say you will not talk about women
again. Really you are still talking about women.
Whatever they may be, it would be better to
leave them alone.
    If you come to Chungking, I will invite
you to dinner.
            Good-bye, Old Friend.

                        Kwong Yoong. Feb. 27th.

Is your family still in Chungking?
....................

2nd Letter :

To brother Kai Bing,

    I tell you one thing. Your tennis racket
and mine are left with Mi Sz. Since our
leaving the Chungking University, we have
never played tennis.
    I tell you another thing. The "resistance"
of the skin of my hands is very strong, it
having touched the connecting points of "150
Volts A.C." and "230 Volts D.C."
    The third thing to tell you is that I
have been a Papa. It may surprise you, but
really somebody has called me Papa. It was many
years ago. I cannot keep it to myself any more
and so I tell you. But you must not make a joke
of me. Good-bye.

            From : Kwong Yoong, Feb. 27th.
pages.zh:
2/2

他认为加入该所是不明智的。然而，我在这一点上不同意他的看法。我们可以在研究所进行大量实验，并利用图书馆增加知识，而且将来还可能获得学位。因此，我希望你下定决心加入研究所。我预计东南联合大学将设立电力研究所，希望阿波（Ah Poh）不要阻止你。
    我觉得我的知识非常有限。我的求学时日越来越少，但我还有很多东西要学。我现在渴望进行实验室实验，以便能有所作为。
    你说你不再谈论女人了。其实你还在谈论女人。不管她们是谁，最好还是离她们远点。
    如果你来重庆，我会请你吃饭。
            再见，老朋友。

                        广荣（Kwong Yoong）。2月27日。

你的家人还在重庆吗？
 ____ 

第二封信：

致凯平（Kai Bing）兄：

    我告诉你一件事。你的网球拍和我的都留在米先生（Mi Sz）那里。自从我们离开重庆大学以来，我们就再也没有打过网球。
    我再告诉你一件事。我手上的皮肤“抵抗力”很强，因为它接触过“150伏交流电”和“230伏直流电”的连接点。
    要告诉你的第三件事是，我已经当爸爸了。这可能会让你惊讶，但确实有人叫我爸爸。那是很多年前的事了。我再也无法保守这个秘密，所以告诉你。但你不能拿我开玩笑。再见。

            来自：广荣（Kwong Yoong），2月27日。

pages.en:
2/3

questioned regarding this letter, Wong Kyi Sing
denies that it is his and states that both Tsuh Sung
(靳強) and Ming Kai Ping (竇開平) have left Shanghai
many months ago, prior to which the latter was a friend
of his and used to sometimes sleep at his home.

Corroboration of the fact that this letter
was written a long time ago was had when same was
presented to the Postal Authorities for examination re
date of posting in Chungking and date of arrival in
Shanghai, the former being 28-2-40 and the latter
5-3-40.

As can be seen this letter other than its
heading contains absolutely nothing of an incriminating
nature, and appears to have been written from one school
student to another merely giving his daily routine.

27 'C...
...
...

John Capilas
D. I.
pages.zh:
2/3

就这封信进行讯问时，王启星（Wong Kyi Sing，原文与前文王啟祥名字略有不同，依原文译）否认这是他的信，并称靳強（Tsuh Sung，音译）和竇開平（Ming Kai Ping，音译）早在数月前就已离开上海，在此之前，后者是他的朋友，并曾有时在他家过夜。

当将此信提交邮政当局检查其在重庆的投递日期和到达上海的日期时，证实了这封信是很久以前写的事实，前者为1940年2月28日，后者为1940年3月5日。

由此可见，这封信除了抬头外，绝对不包含任何具有定罪性质的内容，似乎只是一个学生写给另一个学生的信，仅仅讲述他的日常生活。

27 'C ____ 

约翰·卡皮拉斯（John Capilas）
侦探督察

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 6 a.m. 24-10-41 Sergeant Sato accompanied by
other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters
called at Crime Branch Headquarters and requested assis-
tance to conduct a raid at room No. 318 of the Sun Sun
Hotel, Kwangse Road for the purpose of, if possible,
effecting the arrest of two male Chinese named:-
1. Wang Kyi Sung (王啟琛) and
2. Tsa Ong Ting (查世祥)
who according to information received had arrived from
Kinhwa near Ningpo on September 1st 1941 for purpose of
purchasing Military Supplies on behalf of the Chunking
Government.

Arrangements having been made with Louza Station the
desired assistance was rendered by D.I. Crighton, D.S.
Yamahara, D.I. Seong Ping Tsung and O.D.C. 206.

On arrival at the Sun Sun Hotel, it was ascertained
from the accountant that Room No. 318 had been engaged
in the name of Wang (王) since September 17th 1941, and

协助日本宪兵队

1941年10月24日上午6时，佐藤（Sato）警佐陪同日本宪兵队总部的其他成员来到刑事科总部，请求协助搜查广西路孙孙饭店（Sun Sun Hotel，音译）318号房间，目的是尽可能逮捕两名中国男子：-
1. 王啟琛（Wang Kyi Sung）和
2. 查世祥（Tsa Ong Ting）
据收到的情报，这两人于1941年9月1日从宁波附近的金华（Kinhwa）抵达，目的是代表重庆政府购买军用物资。

在与老闸捕房做出安排后，赖特（Crighton）侦探督察、山原（Yamahara）侦探警佐、宋秉宗（Seong Ping Tsung，音译）侦探督察和第206号外籍巡官提供了所需的协助。

到达孙孙饭店后，从会计处获悉，318号房间自1941年9月17日起以王（Wang）的名义预订，目前有两名为中国男子居住其中。

进入该房间后，逮捕了以下两人：-
1. 王啟琛（Wang Kyi Sung），36岁，四川人，
前大川通（Tung Yi You，音译）轮船公司助理，该公司位于南京路280号，以及

2. Tss Sz Jang (查世祥) 27, Wusin, M/Broker,
residing house No. 1, Lane 10. 6, Lau Dong Ka
Loong Tunging Road
were arrested therein.

A search of this room resulted in the seizure of
25 Miscellaneous Business papers, 16 business cards and
one note Book which contained nothing of an incriminating
nature as far as the allegations made were concerned.

At the request of Sergeant Sato both these persons
were brought to Crime Branch Headquarters where on being
questioned, both emphatically denied being concerned in
any business activities with the Chunking Government,
explaining that they had been in Shanghai for the past 5
and 10 years respectively and that although they were
engaged in Import and Export business they had never to
their knowledge supplied goods to any Military Organisation
under the Chunking Government.

In addition to this they explained that of late
they had purchased a large amount of dyes and sundry
goods, but that as the Customs had banned the export of
these goods they were at present stored in Hardam Godown
and that recently they had attempted to obtain a Japanese
Pass through one named Yih Tse Ching (倪子卿), a notor-
ious loafer who resides in the West Hongkew area and for
the export of these goods to the Kinkwa District, but to
date without result.
pages.zh:
1/2

2. 查世祥（Tss Sz Jang），27岁，无锡（Wusin，音译）人，男，经纪人，
居住于劳东卡龙庭路（Lau Dong Ka Loong Tunging Road，音译）6弄10号1室
在此被捕。

对该房间的搜查结果查获了25份杂项商业文件、16张名片和一本笔记本，就指控而言，其中不包含任何具有定罪性质的内容。

应佐藤警佐的要求，两人被带至刑事科总部，在接受讯问时，两人都坚决否认参与涉及重庆政府的任何商业活动，解释说他们分别在上海已有5年和10年，虽然从事进出口业务，但据其所知，从未向重庆政府下的任何军事组织提供货物。

此外，他们解释说，最近他们购买了大量染料和杂货，但由于海关禁止出口这些货物，目前存放在哈丹仓库（Hardam Godown，音译），最近他们曾试图通过一个名叫倪子卿（Yih Tse Ching）的人获取日本通行证，以便将这些货物出口到金华地区，此人是一个居住在虹口西部地区的 notorious loafer（著名懒汉/无业游民），但至今没有结果。

pages.en:
1/3

They suspect that this man has now given false in-
formation to the Japanese Gendarmerie in re their being
connected with the Chunking Government.

At 8.30 a.m. 24-10-41 Sergeant Sato requested further
assistance to search the office of Wang Kyl Sung (王啟琄)
at 280 Kuikieng Road.

This was agreed to and as result of this search
the following seizures were made:-

1. One Japanese Pass No. 173387 issued to Wang
Kyl Sung on 30th July 1941, authorizing him to
visit Nantao.
2. The photographs, one of which shows Wang Kyl
Sung to be Departmental Chief of the Tseng
Kaung Native Bank, 284 Kuikieng Road.
3. Two Boxes of visiting cards belong to Wang Kyl
Sung giving his occupation as that of Departmen
tal Chief of the Tseng Kaung Native Bank.
4. Sixteen sheets of Examination Papers re Scienti-
fic and Engineering Study.
5. Seventeen Misc. papers, purely of a personal
and business nature, but containing nothing of
an Anti-Japanese nature.
6. Six letters purely of a personal nature.
7. One note Book, containing nothing of a detri-
mental nature.

On return to Crime Branch Headquarters Sergeant
Sato requested the immediate handing over to these two
persons on loan for one week.

This request was refused on the grounds that both
these persons are of quite respectable character and
pages.zh:
1/3

他们怀疑此人现在向日本宪兵队提供了关于他们与重庆政府有关联的虚假情报。

1941年10月24日上午8时30分，佐藤警佐请求进一步协助，搜查王启琄（Wang Kyl Sung，原文拼写变异，依原文译）位于九江路280号的办公室。

此请求获准，搜查结果查获以下物品：-

1. 一张日本通行证，编号173387，于1941年7月30日签发给王启琄（Wang Kyl Sung），授权其前往南市。
2. 照片，其中一张显示王启琄（Wang Kyl Sung）为九江路284号增康钱庄（Tseng Kaung Native Bank，音译）的部门主管。
3. 两盒属于王启琄（Wang Kyl Sung）的名片，注明其职业为增康钱庄（Tseng Kaung Native Bank，音译）部门主管。
4. 十六张科学与工程学考试试卷。
5. 十七份杂项文件，纯属个人和商业性质，不包含任何反日内容。
6. 六封纯属个人性质的信件。
7. 一本笔记本，不包含任何有害内容。

返回刑事科总部后，佐藤警佐要求立即将这两人借押一周。

此请求被拒绝，理由是这两人均具有相当体面的品格，并且

pages.en:
1/4

from all seizures etc made, there was absolutely no evidence
to show that they were in any way concerned in Anti-
Japanese Activities, but were merely conducting their
business as respectable merchants.

In conclusion it has also been ascertained that
between 4 p.m. and 11 p.m. 23-10-41 the man Vik Tsé Ching
(倪子清) who is suspected of having concocted this
case was in the room occupied by the two arrested persons
and during the conversation that took place he ascertained
that the goods held by these two men in Kariam Godown
amounts to between $150,000.00 and $200,000.00.

Instructions are respectfully requested regarding
the disposal of the two arrested men.

John Coghlan
D. I.
pages.zh:
1/4

从所有查获物品等来看，绝对没有证据表明他们以任何方式参与了反日
活动，而只是作为体面的商人经营其业务。

最后还查明，在1941年10月23日下午4时至晚上11时之间，涉嫌捏造此
案的男子倪子清（Vik Tsé Ching）当时身处两名被捕者所居住的房间内，
在随后的谈话中，他获悉这两名男子存放在嘉里安仓库（Kariam Godown）的
货物价值在150,000.00元至200,000.00元之间。

谨请指示如何处置这两名被捕男子。

John Coghlan
侦探督察（D. I.）

One named Tsou Yung Ziang (周文祥) 66, Soochow Widower, Unemployed, residing in the room stated he had arrived from Soochow one month ago to look after the room and contents which belonged to a relative named Zang Tsung Kyib (鄭貞吉) at present in Soochow and working for the Nanking Regime.

He stated Sung Bang Yee might be a friend of his relative but of this he had no knowledge. The Gendarmerie requested Tsou Yung Ziang be temporarily detained at C.B.H.Q. (C.I.) pending enquiries. This was agreed to. (C.I. Memo 531/41)

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 4.20 a.m. on 27-10-41 Sergeant Major Sakai and
four other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie accom-
panied by a male prisoner named Tsang Zee Hong (張治宏)
came to C. B. H. Q. and requested assistance to arrest
two men named Sih (薛), Zah (石) at the Shing Hwa
lodging house, House 3, Lane 112 Fokien Road and
another man named Lieu (刘) in the Dah Shing lodging
house, 108 Haiph Road.

The Gendarmerie prisoner had been arrested in the
Hongkew Area on 26-10-41 on information that he had
transported a pistol and bombs from Taichow to Shanghai,
and according to the Gendarmerie he had implicated the
three wanted men in a terrorist organisation.

Assistance was rendered by D.I. Pryde, D.S.I. Lee
Shu Fah, D.S. Samishima, C.D.S. 40, C.D.C.s 184 and 252.

1

At 7.50 a.m. 27-10-41, 2nd Sub-Lieutenant Yeki
accompanied by other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie
and a Chinese informer came to C.E.H... and requested
assistance to arrest Loh Sui Hsien (陸瑞星) who would
arrive at the Customs Jetty at about 8.15 a.m. to board
a launch for Pootung. The Gendarmerie claimed that this
man had been supplying the Chungking Government with
certain war materials.

Assistance was rendered by A.I. Pryde, J.S.I. Lee
Shu Fah, J.S. Yoshinaga and C.J.C. 206 and a watch kept
on the Bund foreshore near the Customs Jetty.

At 8/15 a.m. the wanted man arrived and was
immediately removed to C.B.H.Q. in the Police Van. On
arrival there he was questioned and it was ascertained
that this man whose name is Loh Sui Hsien is the com-
pradore of Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf Co., Pootung Wharf
Agents, Jardine & Matheson.

On this being ascertained 2nd Sub-Lieutenant
Yeki was asked for further particulars regarding the
offence. 2nd Sub-Lieutenant Yeki was not aware that
this man was the compradore of the said company and
stated according to his information this man had during
1939 and 1940 sent the following material to Chungking
pages.zh:

1

1941年10月27日上午7时50分，二等少尉 Yeki 在其他日本宪兵队成员和一名中国线人的陪同下来到海关缉私局 (C.E.H...)，请求协助逮捕陆瑞星 (Loh Sui Hsien)，此人将于上午8时15分左右抵达海关码头，搭乘小轮前往浦东。宪兵队声称此人一直在向重庆政府提供某些军用物资。

A.I. Pryde、见习巡官李树发 (Lee Shu Fah)、见习巡官 Yoshinaga 和华籍侦探第206号提供了协助，并在海关码头附近的外滩岸线进行了监视。

上午8时15分，通缉犯到达，并立即被警车带至刑事科总部。到达后对其进行了讯问，查明此人名叫陆瑞星，是上海及虹口码头公司、浦东码头代理、怡和洋行的买办。

查明此事后，要求二等少尉 Yeki 提供关于该罪行的更多细节。二等少尉 Yeki 不知道此人是上述公司的买办，并根据其掌握的信息称，此人在1939年和1940年间通过宁波、温州和香港，利用外国船只向重庆发送了以下物资：

pages.en:
1/2

via Ningpo, Wenchow and Hongkong aboard foreign ship :
65 tons of iron, 1600 copper plates, 49 tons
of scrap iron, 8000 railway sleepers.
The Gendarmerie information was to the effect
that more material of this nature was stored in certain
godowns in Pootung.
Loh Sui Helen lives at 8 Balfour Terrace, Avenue
du Roi Albert and has been compradore of the Shanghai
and Hongkew Wharf for the past 21 years.

Geo. B. Simpson.
D. I.
pages.zh:
1/2

65吨铁，1600块铜板，49吨废铁，8000根铁路枕木。
宪兵队的情报显示，更多此类物资储存在浦东的某些仓库中。
陆海伦 (Loh Sui Helen) 住在阿尔伯特王路巴尔福露台8号，担任上海及虹口码头买办已有21年。

Geo. B. Simpson.

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 8 p.m. on the 1st November 1941 Sub-Lieutenant
Hirano and three other members of the Japanese Gendar-
merie Headquarters, Foreign Affairs Branch, came to
H.Q.C.B. C.I. offices and requested assistance to
search an address at 1025 Bubbling Well Road, House 38
Room 12, occupied by one named V.S. Bourmeister, age 50,
Russian, who was arrested by the Gendarmes on the 1st
November 1941 a.m. in Hongkew District on suspicion of
being concerned together with a Japanese in the violat-
ion of Japanese Laws governing the Foreign Exchange
Control and that incriminating documents were expected
to be found in the room.

The necessary assistance was rendered by C.D.C.83
D.S. Yoshinaga and the undersigned and the address given
visited at 8.30 p.m.

A search of the room resulted in seizure of a
number of documents including a Japanese Military Hong
List (Private Issue) and correspondence both in Russian
and English languages.

The seizure,was, at the request of Sub-Lieut
Hirano, handed over to the Gendarmerie for a period of
24 hours, against the usual receipt. (attached)

（左侧手写批注：S/ / E.L. / 3 " H）

1941年11月1日晚上8时，平野 (Hirano) 少尉及其他三名日本宪兵队总部外事支部成员来到刑事科总部刑事侦缉局办公室，请求协助搜查静安寺路1025号38幢12室，该处由一名名为 V.S. Bourmeister 的50岁俄罗斯人居住，他于1941年11月1日上午在虹口区因涉嫌与一名日本人共同违反日本外汇管制法律而被宪兵逮捕，预计在该房间内能找到定罪文件。

华籍侦探第83号、副巡官 Yoshinaga 和签署人提供了必要的协助，并于晚上8时30分前往该地址。

对该房间的搜查导致查获了大量文件，包括一份日军军票清单（私人发行）以及俄文和英文信件。

应平野少尉的要求，查获物品凭常规收据（附后）移交给宪兵队保管24小时。

At 7.50 a.m. on the 2nd November 1941 further
assistance was rendered to Sub-Lieut. Hirano by D.S.I.S
Konovaloff, Yang Shih Kwang and C.D.S. 69 and a female
Chinese named Lee Ah Poh (李阿寶) age 29, native of
Hunan, residing at 1025/38 Bubbling Well Road was
arrested. (C.I. Prisoner No.259/41). She is a common-
law wife of the Japanese prisoner V.S. Bourmeister and
wanted by the Gendarmes for questioning.
Upon instructions of Officer i/c C.I. she was
loaned to the Gendarmerie for a period of 24 hours and
is to be returned together with the documents on the
3rd November 1941.
A receipt is attached.
At the request of the Gendarmerie a watch is
being maintained in the room occupied by the prisoner
by C.D.S. 69 and two Gendarmes.
B'Well station informed and U.S. Marines attended.

A male Chinese alleged to being taken by Japanese

At 5.50 p.m. 9-11-41 one named:
(1) Chang Ngoh Yeong (張鶴云), accountant,
Zang Tsung Lodging House, 118/11,
Chekiang Road and
(2) Koo Kang Ping (陳立華), Transportation
proprietor, No. 47 Zang Tsung Lodging
House, 118/11 Chekiang Road,
came to the station and reported that he had been
informed by one Lee Siau Sung (李少生), that their
friend Wong Yuen Zung (王尚臣) had been taken away
by two unknown male Japanese.

Enquiries by D.S. Rimmer and O.D.C. 298.
When Koo Kang Ping was questioned by detectives
as to whether he had seen Wong Yuen Zung taken away
by Japanese he replied in the negative and stated that
he was only stating what Lee Siau Sung had told him.
Questioned as to where Lee Siau Sung could be
located to substantiate this report Koo Kang Ping stated
that he had left the hotel and had not been seen since.
Detectives visited the Zang Tsung Lodging House
and made enquiries amongst the staff and guests but none
had seen anything unusual occur, and all efforts to
locate Lee Siau Sung failed.

As there was no proof on which to base a report
Chang Ngoh Yeong and Koo Kang Ping were told to go and
try and locate Lee Siau Sung, and bring him to the station
to substantiate this report.

D.D.O. "A" Divn.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / 10 NOV 1941）

一名中国男子据称被日本人带走

1941年11月9日下午5时50分，一名名为：
(1) 张鹤云 (Chang Ngoh Yeong)，会计师，住浙江路118/11号藏宗旅社，和
(2) 陈立华 (Koo Kang Ping)，运输业业主，住浙江路118/11号藏宗旅社47号，
来到捕房报告称，他们从李少生 (Lee Siau Sung) 处得知，他们的朋友王尚臣 (Wong Yuen Zung) 被两名身份不明的日本男子带走。

由巡官 Rimmer 和华籍侦探第298号进行调查。
当侦探讯问陈立华是否亲眼目睹王尚臣被日本人带走时，他予以否认，并称他只是转述李少生告诉他的话。
当被问及在哪里可以找到李少生以证实这一报告时，陈立华称他已经离开旅馆，此后未再见到。
侦探走访了藏宗旅社，并向员工和住客查询，但无人看到任何异常情况，寻找李少生的所有努力均告失败。

由于没有证据作为报告的基础，张鹤云和陈立华被告知去尝试找到李少生，并将其带到捕房以证实这一报告。

“A”区副主管。

1

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 9 p.m. on 9-11-41 Sergeant Sato and other
members of the Japanese Gendarmerie came to C.B.H.Q. and
requested assistance to visit Room No. 47 of the Tsang
Tung Lodging House 118/11. Chekiang Road to arrest one
named Wong Gee Woo (黃聯和) who was adjutant to one
named Wong Woo Zung (王洪臣) Chief of Military
Supplies of the New 4th Army at Kiangying who had been
arrested earlier in the day by the Japanese Gendarmerie
in Hongkew.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

Assistance was rendered by D.I's Pryde and Soong
Ming Tsung, D.S. Sugimoto and C.D.S. 57 . On arrival at
the lodging house it was ascertained from the accountant
named Chang Nyoh Yeong that Room No. 47 had been occupied
by two men named Keo Mang Ping (顧孟平) and Wong Gee
Woo. At about 6 p.m. the accountant had been informed
by Keo Mang Ping that Wong Gee Woo had been called on
to the roadway outside the lodging house and had gone
away in the company of two Japanese dressed in civilian
cloths. It appears that Keo Mang Ping had received this
information from one named Lee Siau Gang (李小生).
Neither Keo Mang Ping or Lee Siau Gang were available at
the time of the visit of the party from C.B.H.Q. (C.I.).

（印：特别科）

督察长 Pryde 和宋明宗 (Soong Ming Tsung)、巡官 Sugimoto 以及华籍侦探第57号提供了协助。到达旅社后，从名为张若英 (Chang Nyoh Yeong) 的会计师处获悉，47号房间由顾孟平 (Keo Mang Ping) 和黄联和两人居住。下午6点左右，会计师接到顾孟平的通知，称黄联和被叫到旅社外的马路上，并与两名身穿便服的日本人一同离开。看来顾孟平是从一名名为李小生 (Lee Siau Gang) 的人那里得到这一信息的。刑事科总部（刑事侦缉局）小组访问时，顾孟平和李小生均不在场。
